label: token right after an early m (m at original position 0 or 1)
explanation: Fires during the original phase on the step right after an input m, but only when that m is at original position 0 or 1 (so t = 1 or 2). The input token at the firing step does not matter. Magnitude: strongest and almost always on when the sequence starts with m (t=1: precision 1.0, ~88% of activation mass, values near max ~2.5). When m is the second token (t=2) it is weaker and fires on only about half such steps, varying with the first token; those steps make up the lowest activation quartile. It does not fire after an m later in the sequence, at t=0, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (one stray activation in 1M steps). Most false positives are t=2 cases that stay silent.

issues: The false positives follow a rule, not noise. All 7821 test FPs are t=2 steps (sequence 'X m ...'), and whether the feature fires there is decided entirely by the first token X. Dev precision of (t==2)&(prev_tok==m)&(first_tok==X) is 1.0 (e: 0.968, 3: 0.982) for X in {e,g,i,l,m,o,q,s,t,w,x,y,z,0,1,3} and 0.0 for X in {a,b,c,d,f,h,j,k,n,p,r,u,v,2}. The explanation's 'about half, depending on the first token' is vague, and the predicate ignores this rule, so test precision is held at 0.766.

The other claims hold. t=1 after m has precision 1.0 (test) and carries 88% of the mass. Nothing fires at t=0, at the delimiter, or at t>=3 in the original phase. There is 1 stray copy-phase activation in each split (0.04 relative). The t=2 steps hold about 12% of the mass.

Small leftover quirk: with the refined predicate, the remaining 40 test FPs are mostly 'e m m' or '3 m m' (a repeated m at t=2), so the claim that 'the input token at the firing step does not matter' has a minor exception.
skeptic.revised_label: token right after an m at position 0, or after an m at position 1 when the first token is in {e,g,i,l,m,o,q,s,t,w,x,y,z,0,1,3}
